title: A Large Scale Investigation of Scaling Limits in Chemical Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2508.13408v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Chemical Language Models (CLMs) are increasingly used in de novo drug design, driven by recent growth in model scale, compute, and dataset size. However, the relationship between design choices, training dynamics, and downstream generation quality remains poorly understood. We present a compute-controlled scaling study of CLMs comprising more than 30,000 experiments across molecular representations (SMILES, SELFIES, SAFE), tokenizations (atom-level and byte-pair encoding), model scales (0.5M-1B parameters), leakage-controlled datasets (MOSES, ChEMBL, PubChem, ZINC-22), and architectures (decoder-only and encoder-decoder). By fitting IsoFLOP profiles, we establish clear scaling trends in pretraining loss, but find that these improvements do not translate into comparable gains in goal-directed molecular design. translated_title: 化学语言模型缩放极限的大规模研究
translated_abstract: 化学语言模型（CLMs）在从头药物设计中的应用日益广泛，这得益于近期模型规模、计算能力和数据集大小的增长。然而，设计选择、训练动态与下游生成质量之间的关系仍然知之甚少。我们开展了一项计算受控的化学语言模型缩放研究，包含超过30,000个实验，涵盖多种分子表示（SMILES、SELFIES、SAFE）、分词方式（原子级和字节对编码）、模型规模（0.5M-1B参数）、防泄漏数据集（MOSES、ChEMBL、PubChem、ZINC-22）以及架构（仅解码器和编码器-解码器）。通过拟合IsoFLOP曲线，我们在预训练损失中确立了清晰的缩放趋势，但发现这些改进并未转化为目标导向分子设计中的相应收益。逐层探测和稀疏自编码器分析揭示了化学表示的持续发展：化学语法……
tldr: 该研究通过超过3万次计算受控实验系统考察了化学语言模型的缩放极限，发现预训练损失随模型规模扩大而持续下降，但这种改进并未带来目标导向分子设计质量的相应提升。
en_tdlr: Through a compute-controlled scaling study of over 30,000 experiments, this work reveals that while pretraining loss in chemical language models consistently improves with scale, these gains do not translate into comparable improvements in goal-directed molecular design.
